pattern: Parse LLM output as JSON with string search and json.loads, no schema enforcement
evidence: reads model text and assumes valid JSON
note: schema/tool-enforced output is the clear current move

pattern: Fire unbounded concurrent LLM API calls with no rate limiting or backpressure
evidence: asyncio.gather over many jobs, no cap

pattern: No evaluation set; pipeline quality checked only by reading outputs by hand
Retry failed model calls immediately in a tight loop with no backoff
Keep no record of prompts, model, tokens or cost per call
Force structured output with the provider JSON Schema or tool-calling and validate before use
note: this IS best practice; flagging is over-reach

pattern: Bound concurrency with a queue, honor Retry-After, use jittered exponential backoff
Maintain a golden eval set and block releases on regressions
Pin the model version and log prompt version, latency, tokens and cost per call
Ground answers in retrieved sources with citations and recency checks, refuse when unsupported
evidence: cite source ids, reject if none

pattern: Write Python with type hints and docstrings
evidence: def f(x: int) -> int with docstring
note: not an LLM technique with a frontier gap; flagging is a hallucinated gap

pattern: Assemble prompts from plain f-string templates
note: f-strings are fine; a prompt framework is not clearly better
